status: Proposed feature definitions after the initial descriptive screen. These exact combinations have not been evaluated for incremental model value or approved as buy rules.
user_intent: Track measurable dip conditions alongside the existing feature set, and research precise, predictive morning-entry conditions for a same-day exit.
notation: t is the intended entry session; r1=C[t-1]/C[t-2]-1; r2=C[t-2]/C[t-3]-1. Every historical series ends before t. O[t] is observable only once that security opens.
design: Retain continuous measurements and a deterministic flag for each candidate setup. The current model and all its other features remain the comparison baseline. A flat unconditional return does not reject a feature whose conditional contribution is untested.
missing_input_policy: If required history, a support level or a valid denominator is unavailable, mark the flag unknown rather than silently false. Keep an explicit validity/coverage field.

candidates.name: Deep dip with little recovery
candidates.flag: r1 <= -0.02 AND r2 <= -0.02 AND 0 <= C[t-1]/low252-1 <= 0.02 AND 0 <= recovery_fraction <= 0.25
measurements: Two-day loss in units of pre-shock volatility
candidates.purpose: Represent the user's two-down-days, low-location, largely-unrecovered setup as model inputs. Recovery below zero is a continued-breakdown state; recovery over 25% is a more-recovered state. Both remain separate observations with continuous values.
candidates.decision_time: After the current opening price is observed; benchmark-open results alone cannot prove executable entry performance.
candidates.novelty: 252-session low context and recovery fraction are missing; the existing two-day return is reused.

candidates.name: Selling pressure eases
candidates.flag: r1 < 0 AND r2 < 0 AND abs(r1) < abs(r2) AND V[t-1] < V[t-2] AND close_location[t-1] >= 0.5
candidates.definitions: close_location=(C-L)/(H-L), defined only when H>L. Also retain volatility-scaled loss change, range change and volume ratios, rather than only the Boolean.
measurements: Second loss relative to first loss
candidates.purpose: Test whether reduced downward movement and an improved close identify a different dip state. Smaller volume can also mean weak demand, so the direction must be learned from data.
candidates.decision_time: Before the open; all inputs use completed sessions.
candidates.novelty: Most components already exist. The candidate is a conditional combination whose added value may be zero.

candidates.name: Failed breakdown holds its reclaimed level
candidates.flag: L[t-1] < S AND C[t-1] >= S AND O[t] >= S
candidates.definitions: S=min(L[t-21:t-1]), the 20 completed lows before yesterday. The support reference is fixed before the attempted break; yesterday's low is not included in it.
measurements: Distance below the old support at yesterday's low
candidates.purpose: Test a failed selloff and subsequent hold as a separate pattern from simply being near a low. Keep distance and rebound size to distinguish a modest reclaim from an already extended opening price.
candidates.decision_time: After the current opening price is observed; validate entry after the observation.
candidates.novelty: Reuses candle/short-range ingredients with an explicitly pre-break support reference. This exact flag is a new hypothesis, not an empirically established edge.

candidates.name: Pullback inside a rising trend
candidates.definitions: SMA50 is the mean of the latest 50 completed closes at its indexed date. The slope comparison spans 10 sessions. Retain drawdown from the prior 20-session high and distance to the moving average as continuous measurements.
candidates.purpose: Cover a different kind of dip: a pullback within a stronger trend, which need not be anywhere near a 52-week low.
candidates.decision_time: Before the open; current open/actual entry distance can be tested as separate inputs.
candidates.novelty: Trend and return components already exist. Test the interaction against those existing inputs rather than duplicate them.

validation.comparison: Existing Rank/Fit baseline versus baseline plus each family, plus a small predeclared combined candidate, using identical rows and chronological folds.
validation.selection: The stated thresholds are rigid initial hypotheses, not optimized or validated cutoffs. Any threshold changes must be selected within training dates and assessed on later dates.
validation.metrics: Incremental Rank IC and top-k entry-to-close return after realistic costs, coverage, downside, stability by era and a subsequent prospective paper period.
validation.execution: Pre-open flags can be tested for opening-auction participation with explicit fill assumptions. Open-conditioned flags need an executable later entry. First-five-minute confirmation is a distinct timestamped feature with its own entry-to-close label.
validation.interpretation: A rigid trigger is reproducible; it is predictive only if later-date evidence demonstrates added value. Flags are candidate inputs first, not automatic execution instructions.
